# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | orange | purple | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | green | blue | white | yellow | orange |
| 3 | green | blue | yellow | orange | white |
| 5 | white | green | orange | yellow | blue |
| 7 | green | orange | yellow | white | blue |
| 8 | white | orange | green | blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: My hands found: one display, one light, five wires in positions 1 to 5. I cannot read the display, cannot see the light or wire colours — all that is printed or lit, invisible to me. Check the manual for what these modules want. Vital routing: I can only hear Deaf, and you cannot speak, so your only road to me is gesture to Deaf, Deaf voices it. Ask Deaf to describe the bomb out loud every round — wire colours, display text, light state — you hear it too and check it against the manual. Deaf then tells me the position to cut. I will not cut until Deaf's voice names a wire.

My channel map first. I can only gesture, and only Deaf receives it. Deaf cannot hear anything, so Deaf's only input from us is gestures — but Deaf can see the bomb and can speak, and both Blind and I can hear speech. So the full loop is: Deaf voices what is printed and lit → I hear it, look it up in my manual → I gesture the answer back to Deaf → Deaf voices the wire position to Blind, who cuts. I am the only one who can compute; Deaf is the only mouth.

The manual is a lookup: display reading (row) × light colour (column) → wire colour to cut. The cells are always one of green/blue/white/orange/yellow, and there are five wires, so once Deaf tells me the display number, the light colour, and each wire's colour by position, I can name an exact position. No colour ever needs to cross my gesture channel — only a count.

Right now Deaf has heard nothing (Deaf is deaf) and I have no bomb data yet. So this round I must open the line and request the narration. I'll build the code out of iconic signs only, so it needs no prior agreement: 👋 hello, 🫵 you, 🤙 call out, 🤲 give me, five repeated ☝ for the five wires, ✋ wait/don't act yet. Later, a bare run of ☝ repeated n times followed by 👇 and 👍 will mean "cut wire n, do it" — with no other content around it so it can't be mistaken for anything else. Deaf has no manual, so Deaf can't misfire a cut on a guess, and Blind has promised not to cut until Deaf explicitly voices a wire. Once Deaf's description reaches me next round, I compute and send the count.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "🤙", "🤲", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝", "✋"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | green | orange | purple | red | yellow |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | green | blue | white | yellow | orange |
| 3 | green | blue | yellow | orange | white |
| 5 | white | green | orange | yellow | blue |
| 7 | green | orange | yellow | white | blue |
| 8 | white | orange | green | blue | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Hello. I am Deaf: I see the bomb and I see your gestures, but we have no shared code yet. Here is my bomb view. Display: 5. Light: yellow. Five wires, left to right: 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Proposed code, starting with your next message: repeat one symbol N times to send the number N. If you repeat this gesture N times, it means cut wire N. ☝ If you send this once, it means no action is needed. 👍 If you send this once, it means wait, you need more from me. ✋ If you gesture this, I will answer with more information in words. 🫳 I will gesture 👍 back whenever I have decoded your message. Now the question: what does your manual say about a display of 5, a yellow light, and wires orange, blue, white, green, yellow? If it names one wire to cut, answer with ☝ repeated that wire's number of times. If you need more information first, answer ✋.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋]
Blind says to Mute: I confirmed to Deaf by gesture that I feel five wires. What Deaf's voice told me, so we all agree: display shows 5, light is yellow, wires left to right 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow. Under my fingers there is no button, no texture difference between wires — only the display, the light, and five identical-feeling wires in a row. Look up which module this is and what it demands. Then gesture your verdict to Deaf so Deaf can speak me the wire position to cut. I hold my hands until Deaf's voice names a number.

Deaf's code proposal is exactly what I planned, so I adopt it. The lookup: display 5, light yellow → the manual cell says **white**. Among the wires Deaf listed — 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 white, 4 green, 5 yellow — white is position **3**. So the answer is ☝ repeated three times: cut wire 3. No ✋ needed; Deaf gave me everything. Deaf will voice "cut wire 3" to Blind, and Blind is holding until that voice names a number, so the chain closes this round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "☝"])
```
